{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java",
      "line": 73,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId",
      "body": "AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) for the rawTokenId argument, so a null rawTokenId is accepted. encodeTokenId would then append null to the token ID and downstream consumers may treat it as a valid raw ID. The check should be performed on rawTokenId."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 33,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "New non-default getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations",
      "body": "OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI interface implemented by grant providers. Adding an abstract method and invoking it during factory initialization breaks source and binary compatibility for any existing custom implementation; older providers will fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError at startup. A default method or optional capability would avoid this."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java",
      "line": 30,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "doc_defect",
      "title": "Shortcut contract says 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2 characters",
      "body": "The Javadoc for getShortcut says shortcuts are usually 3 letters, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider assumes each field is exactly 2 characters and validates a 6-character prefix. A provider returning a 3-character or otherwise malformed shortcut would produce undecodable token IDs. The contract should require exactly 2 characters and validate it."
    },
    {
      "file": "server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java",
      "line": 87,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Removal of OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor is an API break",
      "body": "The public Context(Context) constructor was removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context. Custom grant implementations that created a context by copying an existing one will no longer compile or will fail at runtime. If the removal is intentional, provide a replacement or compatibility path."
    },
    {
      "file": "testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java",
      "line": 483,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring and inverted comparison",
      "body": "The matcher extracts items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) for the grant shortcut and returns false when the value equals the expected shortcut. As a result it does not verify the intended grant prefix and can reject valid values if the wrong position matches. It also does not check that the prefix is long enough before calling substring."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java",
      "line": 113,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Grant shortcut cache updates are not conflict-safe or atomic",
      "body": "getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut add entries to the shared ConcurrentHashMap after a cache miss without checking whether the shortcut or grant ID conflicts with existing entries, and the check-then-put sequence is not atomic. A dynamically discovered grant with a duplicate shortcut can overwrite an existing mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type. Use putIfAbsent/compute and validate uniqueness."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java",
      "line": 54,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Token type is derived from session context client instead of the token's client",
      "body": "getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines lightweight mode via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). If the session context client is not set or differs from the client for which the access token is created, the encoded token type may be wrong or a NullPointerException may occur. The client associated with the client session or the client passed to TokenManager.initToken should be used."
    },
    {
      "file": "services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java",
      "line": 82,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Incorrect-grant test passes by catching RuntimeException from a null factory",
      "body": "DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException broadly. Because the factory is not post-initialized, the decoder path can throw NullPointerException from a null sessionFactory, so the test passes without asserting the intended IllegalArgumentException or validating the decoder. Initialize or mock the factory and assert the exact exception."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Null check validates grantType twice instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: AccessTokenContext constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) for the rawTokenId argument, so a null rawTokenId is accepted. encodeTokenId would then append null to the token ID and downstream consumers may treat it as a valid raw ID. The check should be performed on rawTokenId.

findings.title: New non-default getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is an SPI interface implemented by grant providers. Adding an abstract method and invoking it during factory initialization breaks source and binary compatibility for any existing custom implementation; older providers will fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError at startup. A default method or optional capability would avoid this.

findings.title: Shortcut contract says 3 letters but encoding requires exactly 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc for getShortcut says shortcuts are usually 3 letters, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider assumes each field is exactly 2 characters and validates a 6-character prefix. A provider returning a 3-character or otherwise malformed shortcut would produce undecodable token IDs. The contract should require exactly 2 characters and validate it.

findings.title: Removal of OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor is an API break
findings.body: The public Context(Context) constructor was removed from OAuth2GrantType.Context. Custom grant implementations that created a context by copying an existing one will no longer compile or will fail at runtime. If the removal is intentional, provide a replacement or compatibility path.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong substring and inverted comparison
findings.body: The matcher extracts items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) for the grant shortcut and returns false when the value equals the expected shortcut. As a result it does not verify the intended grant prefix and can reject valid values if the wrong position matches. It also does not check that the prefix is long enough before calling substring.

findings.title: Grant shortcut cache updates are not conflict-safe or atomic
findings.body: getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut add entries to the shared ConcurrentHashMap after a cache miss without checking whether the shortcut or grant ID conflicts with existing entries, and the check-then-put sequence is not atomic. A dynamically discovered grant with a duplicate shortcut can overwrite an existing mapping, causing token IDs to decode to the wrong grant type. Use putIfAbsent/compute and validate uniqueness.

findings.title: Token type is derived from session context client instead of the token's client
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext determines lightweight mode via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session), which reads session.getContext().getClient(). If the session context client is not set or differs from the client for which the access token is created, the encoded token type may be wrong or a NullPointerException may occur. The client associated with the client session or the client passed to TokenManager.initToken should be used.

findings.title: Incorrect-grant test passes by catching RuntimeException from a null factory
findings.body: DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.testIncorrectGrantType catches RuntimeException broadly. Because the factory is not post-initialized, the decoder path can throw NullPointerException from a null sessionFactory, so the test passes without asserting the intended IllegalArgumentException or validating the decoder. Initialize or mock the factory and assert the exact exception.
